title: Questions on Card Age and the Gift Cards & Store Credit Consolidation Move Limit
content:
**How does the age of the stolen or lost card matter?** In a Gift Cards & Store Credit consolidation of value carried onto a card by replacement, the age of the stolen or lost card changes how the move limit is applied. Age is counted in whole months from that card's issue date, shown on its record, to the consolidation date.

| Stolen or lost card issued | How the move limit is applied |
|---|---|
| At least 12 whole months before the consolidation date | The move limit is the whole carried value, in place of the standing limit |
| At least 3 but fewer than 12 whole months earlier | The move limit is multiplied by 1.5 and rounded down to the whole dollar |
| Fewer than 3 whole months earlier | The move limit applies as set |

**What does that give on figures?** (hypothetical move limits as set, before any application for age)

| Move limit as set | Card age | Move limit applied for age |
|---|---|---|
| 100.00 | 5 months | 150.00 |
| 65.00 | 7 months | 97.00 (97.50 rounded down to the whole dollar) |
| 150.00 | 2 months | 150.00 |
| 100.00, carried value 85.20 | 14 months | 85.20 (the whole carried value) |
| 100.00, carried value 240.00 | 12 months | 240.00 (the whole carried value) |

**Where are the edges?** A card issued on 20 January and consolidated on 19 April is 2 whole months old, so the limit applies as set; consolidated on 20 April it is 3 whole months old and the limit is multiplied by 1.5. A card 11 whole months old takes the multiplied limit; at 12 whole months the move limit becomes the whole carried value.
